title: nuc-seq/SNES
scope: Illumina grouped explanatory schematic from individual nuclear genomes through selection, lysis, limited Phi29 amplification, synthesis and the depicted S1 nuclease endpoint labelled DNA. Primary-supported extensions explain the nuc-seq genome/optional-exome library route and the distinct SNES indexed-exome route; these extensions are not drawn in the supplied image. The S1 step remains a family-level depiction with unresolved implementation applicability. The card-only Div-Seq sentence and its commercial-kit list do not define additional implementations here. This is an assay architecture, not an execution protocol or a claim of historical priority.

states.label: Suspension of individual nuclei carrying genomic DNA
features: The far-left Single cell genome icons introduce per-cell genomic material; yellow genome bars have no specified end chemistry. They are explanatory icons, not an extra extraction operation or a depicted transfer into the sorter.
Primary-supported implementation starts with a prepared nuclear suspension before sorting. Nuclei remain separate until one is deposited per well.
Target is nuclear genomic DNA, not RNA or an RNA-derived molecule. Nuclear isolation can omit micronuclear DNA.

states.label: Single selected intact nucleus in its own well
features: G2/M selection is drawn. For a diploid nucleus, this is replicated DNA corresponding to four haploid genome copies; aneuploid nuclei require their corresponding DNA-content peaks.

features: Primary-supported low-input TA ligation library from fragmented WGA DNA that passed amplification QC; this implementation does not require Tn5.

states.label: Pooled, exome-enriched indexed SNES libraries
features: Already indexed DNA libraries are mixed for capture and sequencing; intact nuclei or unlabeled nuclear lysates are not what is pooled at this interface.
Sequenced DNA fragments are amplified copies of nuclear genomic regions enriched for exons; the library barcode retains their single-nucleus association.

Exome enrichment is incomplete and coverage is uneven. The readout supports SNV and indel detection at sufficiently represented sites, with allelic dropout and amplification false positives still possible.

operations.label: Cell sorting from G2/M distribution
operations.description: Retain individual nuclei from the G2/M DNA-content distribution and deposit each into a separate well; crossed-out candidates are not carried forward. The figure calls the examples Cell 1–3, while the paper identifies sorted nuclei. S-phase genome duplication explains the increased input; the scoped selection is G2/M, not selection of S-phase cells.
operations.mechanism: DNA-content flow sorting; primary sources specify DAPI-stained nuclei.
operations.information_effect: Enriches for replicated nuclear genomes while preserving single-nucleus compartment identity. A DNA-content gate is not a guarantee of biological cell-type purity.

operations.information_effect: Extends SNES applicability to non-G2/M nuclei; the input genome-copy advantage of G2/M is absent for this alternative.

operations.label: Phi 29 / Limited amplification
operations.description: Amplify accessible genomic DNA from a single nucleus, producing the first displaced/branched intermediate. Phi29 is the polymerase reagent for this operation, not a separate biological material or a sequenced product.
operations.mechanism: Time-limited isothermal multiple-displacement amplification; SNES explicitly reports modified random hexamer priming.
operations.information_effect: Raises DNA quantity for library construction while copying genomic sequence. Limited amplification is intended to reduce technical error, but it does not establish complete or error-free genome representation.

operations.label: Nuc-seq library construction (paper-supported extension)
operations.description: Convert post-MDA DNA to a sequencing library using the reported alternatives of Tn5 tagmentation or low-input TA ligation construction. These alternatives are kept within one broad library-preparation block; their unshown execution details are not reconstructed. The paper reports this route after MDA and does not establish an intervening S1 treatment.
operations.mechanism: Tn5 simultaneously fragments DNA and attaches sequencing adapters in the reported tagmentation route; the caption separately permits low-input TA ligation library construction.
operations.information_effect: The direct sequencing route samples amplified nuclear genomic DNA broadly and can support genome-wide sequence-variant assessment where covered. It measures genomic sequence rather than transcript abundance.

operations.information_effect: Restricts the intended sequencing target to enriched exonic regions. Capture is selection for a genomic target and does not measure exon expression.

operations.label: SNES barcoded library construction (paper-supported extension)
operations.description: Use WGA DNA that passed amplification QC, fragment it by sonication, and construct a low-input TA ligation library with a sample index unique to the single nucleus. This broad operation establishes the SNES library interface and its difference from the Tn5 route; the unshown QC execution and ligation substeps are not expanded.
operations.mechanism: Fragmented amplified genomic DNA is converted into a TA ligation sequencing library; indexing is introduced during library construction.
operations.information_effect: The index associates subsequent sequence reads with the source single-nucleus library. Genomic copies amplified from the same original molecule are not individually counted by this sample index.

operations.label: Pooling indexed libraries and exome capture (SNES; paper-supported extension)
operations.description: Pool the separately indexed single-nucleus DNA libraries, then enrich for exome targets. The resulting libraries are reported as input to paired-end Illumina sequencing. Pooling is performed on DNA libraries after sample association has been encoded.
operations.information_effect: Sequenced DNA reports nuclear genomic SNVs and indels in captured regions, with nucleus association carried by the sample barcode. Capture does not ensure all exons are represented or that every read is on target; WGA errors and allelic dropout limit interpretation.

method_scopes.rationale: SNES means single nucleus exome sequencing, a distinct implementation rather than an alias for all nuc-seq routes. Its paper supports either G1/0 or G2/M nuclei, limited Phi29 MDA, QC of WGA, low-input TA ligation library construction, per-nucleus barcoding, library pooling and exome capture. Tn5 is not required in this implementation. op_s1 is retained only as the grouped diagram depicts it; applicability to SNES remains unresolved.
